criteria.criterion: studies/firstmate-work-handling/intro.json glossary has entries for 'wake', 'endpoint', 'captain call', 'heartbeat' and 'durable record'. Each has a non-empty claims array of ids that exist in claims.json, or says the firstmate source does not define the term, as 'in scope' does. Verifier compares each definition with the cited claim text in the diff.
criteria.evidence: In the intro.json diff, all five entries are added to the glossary array. Each one opens with 'The firstmate source does not define ...' and cites ids that exist in claims.json: wake [c17], endpoint [c2,c3,c17], captain call [c23,c24], heartbeat [c9], durable record [c19]. I compared each definition with the claim text (Grep of claims.json). Captain call matches c23 (reopen with the deliverable recorded, cleanup never retires the captain's own question). Wake rests on c17's 'stale wake'.

findings.summary: The ship entry still does not cite the claim that says a ship delivers its work as a PR. That is c32, not c33. The earlier verifier and the reading both mixed up the two ids.
findings.evidence: In claims.json, c32 (line 242) says 'a PR-based ship frees its place when its ready PR is recorded'. c33 (line 258) says 'A local-only ship and a scout record no PR'. The candidate added c33, as the criterion asked, but c33, like c37, only implies that non-local ships make PRs. Adding c32 to the ship claims would close the gap the previous minor finding meant to close.

findings.summary: The whole-word match also skips plural and inflected forms, so a card that says 'captain calls' or 'heartbeats' would not be flagged.
findings.evidence: contains_whole_word rejects any match followed by an alphanumeric character, so 'heartbeats' does not count as 'heartbeat'. This does not affect current data, and the five-term list is what was asked for. Allowing an optional trailing 's' would cover plurals.

findings.summary: The test finds the card region by literal HTML markers ('<div class="cards">' and the 'Why it is built this way' heading).
findings.evidence: If that heading text changes, the test panics on unwrap() rather than giving a clear message. That is acceptable for a test, but it is coupled to page wording.

summary: The retry passes: it does everything the last verdict asked for. The firstmate glossary gains entries for wake, endpoint, captain call, heartbeat and durable record. Each says the source does not define the term and cites existing claims whose text supports the entry. The 'ship' entry now opens 'A task that changes a project'. There is a CHANGELOG.md entry in the style of the earlier ones, which fixes the previous major finding. The new tests match whole words ('awake' does not count as 'wake'), use a fixture study to show the check catches missing entries, pass on the real study, and pin the ship <dd> opening with starts_with. Only the test module of xtask/src/site.rs changed, and only files on the deliverables list were touched. Athena's recorded CI shows fmt, clippy and the full test suite passing. My targeted xtask tests and the site build also passed. I could not open the built index.html because policy blocks paths outside the working directory, so the rendered-page checks rest on tests that call the same render() on the real study. One minor point remains: the claim that says a ship delivers its work as a PR is c32, not c33. Both the reading and the earlier verifier mixed up those ids, so the cited support for 'delivered as a PR' is still only implied.
